clinician.final_diagnosis: Foreign body granuloma of the breast from glass shards resulting from prior chest trauma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old asymptomatic female underwent a screening mammogram that revealed calcifications in the skin of the right periareolar breast. Following radiologic localization, a diagnostic incisional biopsy of these calcifications was performed. Histopathology revealed multiple fragments of foreign material consistent with glass shards on a background of scar tissue. Subsequent history taking confirmed the patient had sustained chest trauma in a motor vehicle accident several years prior. Radiologic images of the biopsy specimen showed punctate and pleomorphic calcifications corresponding to the biopsy site. No palpable or visible abnormalities were documented. This constellation of findings supports the diagnosis of a foreign body granuloma from glass fragments introduced during the prior trauma.
